cards.title: AuDHD
cards.subtitle: Overloaded, stuck, or out of spoons
do_first: Bring water and a safe snack
practical: Reduce sensory load: dim lights, quiet the room, offer headphones or a soft blanket
Make decisions instead of asking open questions ("I'm making X for dinner, okay?")
Body-double, or break the task into one tiny next step
Keep safe foods, water, and fidgets within reach
emotional: Don't take stimming, space, or quiet personally
Ask: help, company, or quiet?
Notice small wins, low-key
spiritual: Short, simple prayer
Low-volume worship music if it helps her regulate
say_this: Your brain is out of spoons, not out of worth.
Do you want help, company, or quiet right now?

scripture.note: Fearfully and wonderfully made, brain included.

cards.title: OCD
cards.subtitle: Caught in a loop
do_first: Follow the plan you two agreed on
practical: Use the reassurance/compulsion plan agreed on in a calm moment (and with a therapist if she has one)
Gently redirect to grounding or a different activity
Protect and support treatment time
emotional: Separate her from the disorder
Never react with shock or disgust to intrusive thoughts
The distress is real even when the fear isn't
spiritual: Don't feed faith-based reassurance loops
Pray for peace over her, not for the fear to be answered
say_this: That's the OCD talking, not you.
I know this feels urgent. I'm right here while it passes.
avoid: Giving reassurance outside your agreed plan

scripture.note: Peace that doesn't depend on certainty.

cards.personalize_prompt: Jen: add your agreed reassurance plan here.

cards.title: CPTSD
cards.subtitle: Triggered or on high alert
do_first: Orient her: you're safe, here, today
practical: Know her triggers and early warning signs
Keep things predictable: share plans ahead, no surprises
Grounding help: name date and place, weighted blanket, name things she can see and hear
Always give an easy exit from a situation
emotional: Don't argue with what a flashback makes her feel
Don't take hypervigilance personally
Consistency over time is the medicine
spiritual: God as refuge
Pray for healing with no timeline
Lament is allowed
Honor the cycle-breaking she's doing
say_this: You're safe. You're here with me. It's [today's date].
You don't have to explain. I'm staying.

scripture.note: Refuge and strength, an ever-present help.

cards.title: Depression
cards.subtitle: Heavy, empty, or hopeless
do_first: Take one task off her plate
Tell her she's not a burden
practical: Handle meals, dishes, laundry, and business tasks like client visits and messages
Low-bar invites: five minutes outside, starting the shower for her
Help with meds and appointments if she wants
Open curtains, fresh air, a short walk together
emotional: Presence over solutions
Keep checking in even if she says little
No "just think positive"
spiritual: Carry faith for her when she can't feel it
Read Psalms of lament together
Never link depression to weak faith
say_this: You're not a burden to me. I'm glad to be here.
You don't have to do anything right now. I've got it.
avoid: Leaving her alone for long stretches

scripture.note: Why, my soul, are you downcast? Honest faith.

safety.trigger: If she mentions hopelessness, not wanting to be here, or hurting herself
safety.action: Ask her directly and calmly, stay with her, and help her reach professional support. In the US, call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline), or call 911 if she's in immediate danger.

cards.title: PMS / PMDD
cards.subtitle: Hormonal lows, irritability, pain
signs: Near that time in her cycle
practical: Track her cycle together to see hard days coming
Stock comfort items ahead: heating pad, snacks, pain relief, cozy clothes
Pick up extra chores that week
emotional: The feelings are real, even if the timing is hormonal
Don't take irritability personally; save hard talks for later
Remind her it will lift
spiritual: Remind her to give herself grace
Pray for rest and peace in her body
say_this: This is a hard week, not a hard you.
It's lifted before and it will again. I'm here till it does.

scripture.note: Weeping for a night, joy in the morning.

cards.title: Shutdown
cards.subtitle: Complete overwhelm, non-verbal
practical: Cut input immediately: lights, noise, questions
Use non-verbal signals: thumbs up/down, hand squeeze, text, or Tend's one-tap buttons
Quietly bring water and a blanket
Handle anything outside: calls, clients, visitors
emotional: No demands for words or eye contact
Quiet presence, nearby or in the room, her choice
Afterward, no interrogation
It's overwhelm, not rejection
spiritual: Silent prayer; hand on her back if touch is okay
Soft instrumental worship if it helps
say_this: You don't need to talk. Squeeze my hand if you want me to stay.
I'm handling everything else. Take all the time you need.
avoid: Treating it as the silent treatment

scripture.note: The Spirit prays with wordless groans. No words needed.

cards.title: Shame
cards.subtitle: Feeling like I am bad
practical: Interrupt the spiral: step outside, change rooms, work alongside her
Help repair a real mistake so it stops looming
Quietly handle the thing she feels ashamed about
emotional: Stay close; shame expects abandonment
Share his own imperfections
No jokes at her expense right now
spiritual: Speak her identity in Christ over her
Pray a blessing over her by name
say_this: You made a mistake. You are not a bad person.
I'm not going anywhere.

cards.title: Rejection Sensitivity
cards.subtitle: Feeling rejected or too much
practical: Be clear, not vague
When he needs space, say why and when he'll be back
Follow through; text if running late
emotional: Reassure before she has to ask
Never call it an overreaction
Remind her he chose and keeps choosing her
spiritual: Remind her she's accepted in the Beloved
Pray against the lie of too much / not enough
say_this: I'm not upset with you. I just need 20 minutes to decompress.
I choose you. Today too.

cards.title: Betrayal Trauma
cards.subtitle: Trust feels unsafe
practical: Offer the transparency you've agreed on without being asked
Keep words and actions consistent, especially in small things
Answer questions without defensiveness, even repeated ones
emotional: Triggers aren't accusations
Her caution makes sense
Steady beats perfect
spiritual: God is faithful even when people aren't
Forgiveness and rebuilding trust are separate; neither is rushed
say_this: Your caution makes sense. I'll be patient with it.
Ask me anything. I'm not going to get defensive.

scripture.note: His mercies are new every morning.

cards.title: Low Self-Esteem
cards.subtitle: Feeling not enough
practical: Specific compliments tied to real things she did
Back her goals with action: show up, review her projects, cheer
Celebrate her wins out loud, including in front of others
emotional: Affirm character and effort, not just looks
Tell her what he admires, unprompted
spiritual: Read identity scripture over her (Psalm 139, Ephesians 2:10)
Pray blessing and purpose over her
Remind her she's a cycle-breaker
say_this: Hey, that's my wife you're talking about.
Breaking cycles takes strength most people never see. You have it.

scripture.note: He rejoices over you with singing.
